newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks up in morning trade on rate optimism.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks up in morning trade on rate optimism.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded higher on Wednesday morning, lifted by optimism about U.S. interest rates, traders said.
The Hang Seng Index was up nine points or 0.07 percent at 13,557. Turnover was HK$1.52 billion after the first half-hour of trade.
"Interest rates are beginning to move in the right direction in the U.S.," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.
The U.S. Federal Reserve ends its two-day policy-setting meeting on Wednesday and is expected to leave rates unchanged.
Traders said they expect activity to remain quiet ahead of the Chinese Lunar New Year holiday.
"I don't think there will be much excitment in the market today," said Pricilla Ng, executive director of CEF GC Brokerage Ltd. "Trading is normally quiet approaching the Lunar New Year holiday."
The market will be closed on Thursday and Friday.
China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd made its debut on Wednesday, opening at HK$1.50 per share compared with an issue price of HK$1.38. The shares later fell back to HK$1.43.
"The shares started off higher, in line with the grey market price," said Kent Rossiter, Nikko Securities institutional sales manager. "It then settled to about the HK$1.40 level."
"It gives the chance for investors to hold the shares without making a loss," he said. "But I don't think they can make a quick profit either if they sell the stock now."
Rossiter said he expects the market to remain range-bound after the Chinese New Year holiday.
"I don't think the market will be trying new highs immediately after the Chinese New Year," he said.
Trading in shares of Peregrine Investments Holdings and Kwong Sang Hong International Ltd was suspended on Wednesday at the companies' request pending an announcement.
"It was just a formality for Peregrine to complete acquiring Kwong Sang Hong," Rossiter said.
Peregrine Investments said in December it would privatise Kwong Sang Hong, offering 200 Peregrine shares plus HK$1,700 cash for every 1,000 Kwong Sang Hong shares.
HSBC Holdings was up HK$1.00 at HK$183.00 and Hang Seng Bank gained HK$1.00 to HK$92.50. REUTER
